statement: A config key is matched case-insensitively and only at the start of a line, directly followed by `:`. Leading and trailing blanks and CRs are stripped first. A `#` line therefore never holds a key.
quote: "if (!strncasecmp(&config[i], key, key_len) && config[i + key_len] == ':') { if (i && config[i - 1] != SEPARATOR)"
host_value: keys are lower-case, indented by 2 or 5 spaces

statement: The keys that take a path are `path` and its aliases `kernel_path`/`image_path`, plus `module_path`, `dtb_path`, `global_dtb`, `wallpaper` and `term_font`. A `#...` inside `cmdline` or `comment` is not a pin.
The hash is everything after the **last** `#` of the URI, so a `#` inside a file name is part of the path. It must be exactly 128 hex characters, in either case; anything else is a URI error.
The hash is BLAKE2b-512 over the file as stored on the partition. For a gzip (`$`) resource it covers the compressed bytes and is checked before decompression.
quote: "the hash covers the whole file as stored on disk (its compressed bytes, including anything after the gzip data)"

statement: On a mismatch Limine panics unless `hash_mismatch_panic` is `no` (case-insensitive). The value is read from the first occurrence in the file. With `no`, it prints a warning and waits: `Y` (or `y`) boots the file anyway, and any other key returns to the menu.

Secure Boot with an enrolled config hash forces panic and turns off the editor. Without an enrolled hash, Limine treats Secure Boot as inactive. A wallpaper or font that fails is skipped (optional resource), in either mode.
quote: "Forced to `yes` when Secure Boot is active and a config hash is enrolled."

statement: `objcopy` given only an input file rewrites that file. Even `--dump-section`, which only reads a section out, rewrites the UKI it reads, and the BLAKE2b of the whole file changes. Probe with an explicit output file, or not as root on `/boot` at all.
source: S354 section `infile outfile` (raw HTML lines 188-191 and 634 of the pinned snapshot)
quote: "If you do not specify outfile, objcopy creates a temporary file and destructively renames the result with the name of infile."
